chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever washes his hands before eating and after eating, he will live in ease and be cured of affliction in his body."

key_terms.سَعَةٍ: Ease, spaciousness, or comfort in life

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of washing hands before and after eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the physical act of handwashing to broader metaphysical well-being, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the unity of bodily purity and spiritual ease. The promise of 'ease' (sahh) suggests not only freedom from disease but also a state of contentment and reduced worldly anxiety, while protection from 'affliction' (balwa) underscores the divine care for the believer’s physical vessel.
